headings.title: SMTO-EML-0009 — SMTO couldn't use a file you asked it to attach

html:
SMTO-EML-0009 — SMTO couldn't use a file you asked it to attach

GUID: 3bffea84-91c2-58d3-a189-8a41f6122b20
Slug: email-attachment-not-found
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • One of the attachments isn't a file SMTO may use in this conversation, no longer exists, or has a name or file type SMTO can't use. The email wasn't sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Add the file to the conversation again with the Add context button in the message box, or point SMTO to a file it created earlier in this same conversation. SMTO only attaches files that have been shared in, or created by, this conversation.
  2. Make sure the file's name isn't blank and has no slashes (/ or ). Rename it if needed before adding it again. SMTO refuses file names that could point to another folder, to keep your files safe.
  3. Ask SMTO to send the email again with that attachment. SMTO looks up attachments fresh each time, and this check happens before anything is sent.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the mail server accepted the message, and recipients receive the attachment.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, saying which file you tried to attach and where it came from.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Attachment resolution found no eligible granted artifact, conversation upload or Gateway temporary-file reference, the filename or MIME type was invalid, or the approval preview could not look up the referenced attachment.

What this means

  • Attachment resolution lacks an eligible granted reference, filename/MIME syntax is invalid, or confirmation cannot retrieve exact attachment bytes. Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.

Why this can happen

  • Attachment resolution lacks an eligible granted reference, filename/MIME syntax is invalid, or confirmation cannot retrieve exact attachment bytes.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the grant, reference, filename and MIME type; absolute paths only work through eligible Gateway temporary-file publication.

How to fix it

  • Use an attachment ref that resolves through the existing grants: artifact:// or art_ references, context:// or ctx_ conversation uploads, or an absolute path eligible for the Gateway's temporary-file publication. Correct rejected filenames (empty, '.', '..', or containing / or ) and MIME types that do not match type/subtype.
  • Select an existing granted artifact/upload or an eligible Gateway temporary-file reference, then correct any rejected filename or MIME type.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • Each intended attachment resolves to granted exact bytes with a valid filename/type.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
